notes: Play knowledge rewritten as executable actions. Every reference is checked against the generated level data by tools/gen_level_nuance.py.

Aztec is a bonus level and plays like one: both objectives are item uploads at fixed terminals, and the real content is a boss who cannot be out-shot in the open. It is the clearest case in the game of geometry beating firepower.

nuance.claim: The guidance objective is completed by equipping the data item and using it on a disk reader, so there is nothing to shoot and no amount of combat advances it.
The disk reader sits behind bulletproof glass on a desk, so the approach is to the console rather than to the drive that is visible through it.
The launch objective is a separate item used on a different set of computers, so completing the guidance upload does not put the shuttle any closer to launching.
The shuttle cannot be launched before its guidance is reprogrammed, so the two objectives are a fixed sequence rather than a pair.
nuance.because: The level has exactly two objectives and the launch is the terminal one.

nuance.claim: Using the launch data starts a countdown, so anything still wanted from the level has to be collected before that point.
The boss cannot be traded with in the open; the fight is won by staying out of his firing line using the stairway area, where he cannot bring his weapons to bear.
He only fires along a clear straight line, so breaking line of sight stops incoming damage entirely rather than merely reducing it.
Killing the boss starts continuous enemy spawning, so where he dies decides how much pressure the rest of the level is done under.
Because the spawning begins where he dies, he is led away from the terminals first so the objectives can be finished ahead of the reinforcements.
The boss absorbs a great deal of damage, so the fight is planned around having enough ammunition rather than around a particular weapon.
